 Hasan's hat-trick puts Bangladesh in command of Afghanistan Test 
 Hasan Mahmud, fresh from his nine-wicket haul in Bangladesh’s upset of Australia at Darwin in August, finished with 5-55 to dismiss Afghanistan for 240.
 Updated : Oct 16, 2026 01:25 IST , ABU DHABI - 2 MINS READ

 Fast bowler Hasan Mahmud took a hat-trick to help put Bangladesh into a commanding lead over Afghanistan in the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi on Sunday.
 The 26-year-old, fresh from his nine-wicket haul in Bangladesh’s upset of Australia at Darwin in August, finished with 5-55 to dismiss Afghanistan for 240 at Sheikh Zayed Stadium.
 Afghanistan skipper Rahmat Shah hit a gritty 105 not out but did not get enough support to match Bangladesh’s first-innings 346.
 ALSO READ | Screws in his foot, surgery behind him, Rohit Sharma returns with five wickets 
 With a first-innings lead of 106, Bangladesh consolidated its position with 223-6 at close on day three, a lead of 329 runs with four wickets intact.
 At the close, Litton Das was unbeaten on five and Mehidy Hasan Miraz yet to get off the mark, giving Bangladesh a sniff of victory on a weary pitch.
 Tiger of the Day! Hasan Mahmud delivers a fifer and a hat-trick in the Only Test against Afghanistan. 🇧🇩🔥
#Bangladesh #Tigers #HasanMahmud #TestCricket https://t.co/LxrUrusrIi
— Bangladesh Cricket (@BCBtigers) October 11, 2026 Resuming at 211-4, Afghanistan was dismantled by Hasan.
 He dismissed Ismat Alam, Qais Ahmad and Zia-ur-Rehman in successive balls to leave Afghanistan 220-8.
 Hasan became only the third Bangladesh bowler after Alok Kapali (2003) and Sohag Gazi (2013) to take a Test hat-trick.
 He also now has four five-wicket hauls.
 “I am delighted to take a hat-trick and more than that it’s good to help the team get a strong position from where we can force a victory,” he said.
 Hasan’s pace partner Ebadot Hossain finished with 4-56.
 The Afghan captain Rahmat hit 10 fours and two sixes in his fourth Test hundred.
 When Bangladesh batted for the second time, skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto with 82 and veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahim with 81 lifted them from 53-3 with a 159-run stand for the fourth wicket.
 Pacers Yamin Ahmadzai (2-42) and Zia-ur-Rehman (2-55) shared the bowling honours for Afghanistan.
